text:
Maria: Heads up — saw multiple 30–60s tail latency spikes this morning when GPUs scale-to-zero and then have to cold-start for short bursts. Any quick wins? :thinking:
Devin: Yup, saw it in eu-west. Pod backlog spiked while new GPU nodes booted. Requests got re-routed but still bad UX.
Kai: Current CA flags we use: --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m, --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m, --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5. That means nodes can go to 0 if no pods for ~10m.
Sarah: My gut: we need a tiny warm pool per zone (1 small GPU node) so short bursts hit warm nodes. Cost vs latency tradeoff though.
Maria: Agreed. Proposal: warm-pool of 1 per zone + cooldown so we don't churn. Something like:
```yaml
nodePool:
  name: gpu-pool
  autoscaling:
    minSize: 0
    maxSize: 12
  warmPool:
    minWarm: 1  # keep one warm
    cooldownSeconds: 300
```
Not real k8s native, but we could implement with an autoscaler wrapper or cloud provider feature.
Devin: Alternatively mark nodes as "protected" for scale-down and run a tiny pod that pins them (cheapish) — e.g., a low-priority model-cacher DaemonSet that keeps the GPU drivers warmed and a tiny heartbeat so CA sees usage.
Kai: Yeah, we did something like that for CPU pools. DAEMONSET trick works: a low-resource pod with qos=burstable touching /dev/nvidia* so kube sees node as used. Downside: billing still counts GPU minutes.
Sarah: Cost question: if we keep 1 warm per zone across 3 zones that's 3 GPUs idle — can we use preemptible/spot for warm nodes? Might kill them mid-burst.
Maria: Thoughts: mix of strategies — prefer spot warm nodes + fallback policy that routes requests to non-GPU model variant if warm node preempted. Also keep a 60–120s cooldown before scale-to-zero to catch short bursts.
Kai: For CA config, shorten scale-to-zero but extend "grace" via a custom metric (queue length or recent RPC rate). Example: feed "recent_requests_per_minute" to HPA/CA so nodes stay up while traffic is spiky.
Devin: Operational notes: ensure kubelet eviction thresholds and driver startup not delaying pod readiness. Driver init can be 10–20s on some images; we should bake optimized AMIs with preinstalled drivers + cached libs.
Sarah: Also consider a model-side warmup: preload model artifacts into host cache on node provision so cold-start only needs container start, not model download. Use an init container that runs on node add.
ops-oncall: Adding runbook checklist: monitor: gpu_node_warm_count, pod_backlog, cold_start_latency. Alert if cold_start_latency > 20s for >5m. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-warmup
infra-bot: autoscaler: scheduled scale evaluation at 1719001500, decided to keep 1 warm node in eu-west-1 for now. :white_check_mark:
Maria: OK next steps: 1) Kai + Devin prototype warm daemon (DaemonSet) that pins nodes and reports cost estimate; 2) Sarah tests spot fallback and model cache; 3) ops-oncall add alert. I'll make a quick RFC in docs.
Devin: I'll prototype this afternoon, will post results here.
Kai: I'll prepare a small AMI with drivers + cached model layers and share bake script.
Sarah: I'll run a quick cost projection for 1 vs 2 warm nodes per zone and post.
Maria: Thanks team. If we can shave the cold tail from 60s-><10s it's a big UX win. :rocket:
